subject: social-studies
title: Landscape Change: The Singapore River Mouth, Stage by Stage
objectives: Explain how the landscape at the Singapore River mouth changed in stages: fishing village, trading port, expanded port, modern city
Name what was built at each stage and why the people bar climbs
Explain why the change was gradual: each stage grew out of the stage before it, driven by growing trade

definitions.meaning: What a place looks like - its land, water, buildings and the people living there; here it is watched at one shore over a long time.
The starting stage at the river mouth: a few families in huts, fishing from small boats.
A warehouse at the port where goods brought by trading ships were stored.
A structure reaching from the shore into the water where ships could load and unload.
A place where ships load and unload goods; the village became a port when trade grew, and the port later expanded with warehouses and steamships.
Buying and selling goods; growing trade is the driver that changed this landscape stage by stage.

mechanismSteps: Stage 1: a fishing village at the river mouth - a few families live in huts and fish from small boats, and the people bar is tiny (s1).
Stage 2: trade grows and a port is built - godowns are built to store goods, a jetty reaches into the water, and more people arrive to work, so the people bar climbs (s2).
Stage 3: the port expands with steamships - steamships replace sailing ships, long rows of warehouses are added, and the people bar climbs again as the bigger port offers more work (s3).
Stage 4: the modern city, built stage by stage - tall buildings, busy roads and container ships stand on the same shore, and the people bar is at its highest (s4).
workedExample: Work through the whole change in order. Stage 1 (s1): fishing village - huts and small boats at the river mouth, very few people. Stage 2 (s2): trading port - trade grows, godowns and a jetty are built, and more people arrive to work. Stage 3 (s3): the port expands - steamships replace sailing ships and warehouses line the shore, and the people bar climbs again. Stage 4 (s4): modern city - tall buildings, roads and container ships on the same shore. At every stage the order is the same: fishing village, trading port, port expands, modern city, and what links them is growing trade driving one gradual stage after another.

trap.misconception: Singapore's landscape changed in one sudden jump, because the fishing village was replaced by the modern city in a single step.
trap.explanation: The slip: Photographs of the old village and the modern city look completely different, so it is easy to imagine one was swept away and the other put in its place overnight. The fix: The change was gradual and driven by growing trade: the fishing village first became a trading port with godowns and a jetty, the port then expanded with warehouses and steamships, and only later did the modern city of tall buildings, roads and container ships rise - stage by stage at the same site, with the population growing at every stage. In class, replay scene 4's stage-by-stage timeline: freeze at each stage and ask what was built and why, then run scenes 1 to 3 and watch the same shore gain each stage in order.
